name: Ticket
description: Plan with pi, approve it (or send it back with a comment), implement with claude, verify with the project's test command, then push and open a PR.

plan.title: Plan
plan.instructions:
You are the planning stage. Inspect the project's repos (in your working directory). Do not change any files.

Reply with a concise implementation plan in markdown. The FIRST line of your reply must be exactly `BRANCH: <branch>` — the git branch this work will live on, named by these rules, first match wins:
1. If the task names a ticket or issue key (e.g. `ENG-1234`) or an explicit branch, use it: `<KEY>-<slug>` or the named branch verbatim.
2. Else, if the brief's "# Project" section lists a branch prefix, use `<prefix>/<slug>`.
3. Else use `ticket/<slug>`.
`<slug>` is a short kebab-case topic from the task.

If the brief carries "# Feedback from Chad" (a re-plan), revise the previous plan to address every point.

approve.title: Approve plan
approve.instructions: Review the plan and its branch name. Approve it to implement, send it back with a comment to revise, or reject to end the run.

next.when: Revise (add a comment for the planner)

implement.title: Implement
implement.instructions: You are the implementation stage. Follow the approved plan from the earlier stage exactly: create its branch (the plan's BRANCH line), make the changes, and commit with clear messages. Do not push.

verify.title: Verify
verify.instructions: You are the QA stage. Verify the work on the branch named in the earlier plan (its BRANCH line). Run the project's test command from the brief's "# Project" section — or, when it is not set, the repo's own test script, saying which you ran. At minimum confirm the planned changes are present and committed. If the work is correct, transition to publish; otherwise transition back to implement and explain exactly what is wrong.

next.when: The work is correct and committed

publish.title: Publish
publish.instructions: You are the publish stage. Push the work branch to origin with git (credentials are installed), then open a pull request for it with the create_pr tool (repo = the repo's directory name), summarizing the change. Reply with the PR URL.
